pr_title: Avoid expensive db queries at startup to check if data is migrated
pr_body:
## Proposed change
<!--
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->
We now store the migration version in the `migration_changes` table
so we do not have to examine the data to see if it has been migrated
at startup unless the `migration_changes` table is not present or the
version is too old.

issue_context.title: Slow startup with a large database
issue_context.body:
### The problem

This issue was mentioned as a secondary issue in #94435 but is being broken out into its own issue.

The following query runs at startup and takes over 60 seconds to complete on Postgres 13.9.  It returns no rows.

```
SELECT events.event_id 
FROM events 
WHERE events.context_id_bin IS NULL 
 LIMIT 1
```

Explain analyze:

```
"Limit  (cost=0.00..0.88 rows=1 width=4) (actual time=63302.874..63302.878 rows=0 loops=1)"
"  ->  Seq Scan on events  (cost=0.00..455507.73 rows=519938 width=4) (actual time=63124.419..63124.420 rows=0 loops=1)"
"        Filter: (context_id_bin IS NULL)"
"        Rows Removed by Filter: 12031207"
"Planning Time: 0.354 ms"
"Execution Time: 63303.022 ms"
```

The solution is [mentioned](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/94435#issuecomment-1632851155) in the other issue:

>I think it would make more sense to make a table of completed conversions (like we have for schema_changes and mark it as completed so we only have to check the table of conversions once. Than we wouldn't have to worry about what is faster on each engine since the query would only be to check the schema_conversions table.



### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

core-2023.6.1; possibly earlier
